newsitem.title: USA: Oregon House OKs bill backing school district debt.
newsitem.headline: Oregon House OKs bill backing school district debt.

text.p: Oregon's House unanimously approved a bill that would reduce school district borrowing costs by allowing schools to use the state's bond rating when issuing debt, state Treasurer Jim Hill said on Wednesday.
The legislation, introduced by Hill, would allow districts to use the state's AA-rating, which is higher than most rural and small school district bond ratings, the treasurer said.
The state's general fund would back the school district bonds, and pay bondholders should a district go into default, Hill's office said.
School districts with bond ratings below AA would be eligible to participate in the program, Hill's office said.
The legislation was introduced in response to voter-approved initiatives limiting the ability of Oregon school districts to impose new or raise existing taxes.
The bill, called the Oregon School Bond Guaranty Act, could save Oregon schools $5 million in the first year alone and as much as $22 million in the first five years, Hill said.
"With the school budget as tight as it is, any amount of savings will be critical for many districts," Hill said in a statement.
"(The bill) will allow schools to use that savings as additional resources to enhance the quality of elementary and secondary education in Oregon," Hill added.

The bill now advances to the state Senate for review. If approved by the Senate and signed by the governor, the Oregon School Bond Guaranty Act would appear on the November 1998 statewide ballot for voter approval.
